description.narrative: The project is implemented in Turkey. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy &amp, human rights, gender equality and peace and conflict. The main right holders are academics, researchers, students, journalists, writers and women. Through capacity buildning, mobilising, trainings and seminars, networks and advocacy the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between the local partner organisation Ismail Besikci Foundation in Istanbul, the Social Democratic Women in Sweden (S-Women Vsterbotten) and the Palme Center. The local partner organisation Ismail Besikci Vakfi is a foundation working with primarily for freedom of expression, specifically for academic freedom, with a specific focus on the kurdish question. The S-kvinnor Vsterbotten, one of the Palme Center's member organisations, is highly engaged in the development in Turkey, with a memberbase intrested in contribution to the democratic development. They support this partnership with their specific focus on and expertise in gender equality. The Palme Center will support the project with administrative and technical support.Other Donors to the OrganisationThere is no other donors in the project.Project ObjectiveThe project's objective is to contribute to the development of an open, plural society and a culture of democracy where human rights including the freedom of expression, ethnocultural rights as well as gender equality are respected and social tensions and conflicts are solved amicably with mutual respect without resorting to violence.Actor groupsThe organisations main actors within the group of, 1) right holders are: academics, researchers, students, journalists, writers, politicians and those marginalized, persecuted or prosecuted due to their critical political views. 2) actors working in cooperation: the academic trade unions, student organisations and associations, national and international NGOs and human rights activists working on human rights, labour rights and academic freedoms and freedom of expression. 3) decision makers: the government agencies working on human rights and labour rights such as the Ministry of Labour and Social Security, Human Rights Inquiry Committee, Provincial Human Rights Committees, Ombudsman, Turkeys Human Rights and Equality Institute, as well as universities and other academic institutions, the inter-governmental, supranational organisations within the UN, European Union, Council of Europe and OSCE with a mandate for the realisation of fundamental human rights, democracy and rule of law in Turkey.
